  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type

          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'

        title:

          example: NoResourceFoundException

        status:

          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600

          example: 500

          title: Detail

          type: string

          readOnly: true

          title: Timestamp

            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title

        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message

      properties:
        firstName:

          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to E.164
            form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped, a leading '+' and country code
            are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must be a '+'
            followed by 8 to 15 digits; that canonical value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:

          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household

            shares a household with an existing owner. When true, the create is allowed

## Summary

The codebase already rejected same-household duplicates and had a `sharesHousehold` flag that allowed the create. I added the missing piece: assigning and returning a shared, stable `householdId`.

**What I changed:**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — Added a read-only `householdId` string to the `Owner` schema (returned, not part of create input), so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes it.

2. **`Owner` entity** — Added a persisted `household_id` column with getter/setter (needed because `GET /api/owners/{id}` re-reads from the DB).

3. **DB schemas** (h2, hsqldb, mysql, postgres) — Added the `household_id` column. Tests run on hsqldb.

4. **`HouseholdMatcher`** (new) — Single home for household logic: the lenient last-name + address normalization (extracted from the old duplicate checker so it's not duplicated), `findMembers(candidate)`, and a deterministic `householdId(candidate)` derived from the normalized key (so every member resolves to the identical value — a genuinely stable shared identifier).

5. **`HouseholdDuplicateChecker`** — Slimmed to delegate to `HouseholdMatcher` (`isDuplicate = members not empty`), removing the copied normalization code.

6. **`HouseholdAssigner`** (new) — Tags the new owner with the shared id and back-fills the same value onto existing members that lack one, so "both" owners end up carrying the identical `householdId`.

7. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — When the owner duplicates an existing household: reject unless `sharesHousehold` is set; otherwise assign the shared household id before saving.

8. **`OwnerMapper`** — Ignored `householdId` on the `OwnerFields → Owner` mapping (it's server-assigned), matching the existing pattern.

Each unit keeps a single responsibility: matching/deriving is read-only in `HouseholdMatcher`, the duplicate check and the assignment are thin components over it, and the controller just orchestrates. Full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`).
